question: How does PhyMo both prevent canonical appearance from acting as a motion shortcut and enforce temporally coherent motion evolution?
answer: PhyMo gates canonical appearance updates using a per-Gaussian motion-confidence gate based on active local motion, and it imposes bidirectional kinematic continuity by requiring motion states from neighboring timestamps to be consistent when propagated to the same observation time.

quotes.text: In this way, canonical appearance is no longer a fully free shortcut channel; instead, its effective update is guided by whether the corresponding Gaussian already exhibits active local motion.

Specifically, for each observed timestamp t, the motion states predicted at t_{l}=t-\Delta t and t_{r}=t+\Delta t are required to remain consistent when propagated toward the same observation time through the kinematic chain from acceleration to velocity and from velocity to displacement.
